There is a right answer, but it doesn't fit into a soundbite.

Right now, absolutely no taxpayer dollars (at a federal level anyway) go to Planned Parenthood's family planning. In fact, under existing scrutiny, they've even separated out the charities into separate legal entities which share the rent at clinics. 3% of services provided at Planned Parenthood are abortion, ~30% are birth control, and the rest are all preventative medicine: mammograms, HIV screening, pap smears, etc.

As it stands, the only federal funding Planned Parenthood receives is for preventative health. It gets those grants because while a hospital might charge $400 for a simple procedure, Planned Parenthood bills the government at cost, and its costs are very low (physicians and nurses typically make far less than what they'd make in private practice). To make absolutely sure that no government money is used for anything even related to abortions, they even have separate corporate charters, separate supplies, separate exam rooms, separate payroll, etc.

So to even pro-life Democrats, it doesn't make any more sense to defund Planned Parenthood's HIV screening program than it does to defund another clinic for existing in the same office building. But since that doesn't fit into a soundbite, and "Defund Planned Parenthood" does fit into a soundbite, Democrats are in kind of a pickle on what to do: throw the most effective, cheapest, and most efficient HIV screening and mammogram charity under the bus for political reasons, or stick by women (and men's) health despite the political consequences?

As the guy in charge of our households network, another bit that concerns me is that Wi-Fi Sense is enabled by default. Wi-Fi Sense is a feature that will save the password of any wireless networks you join, and upload them to Microsoft's servers, then automatically share it with all of your Facebook, Outlook, and Skype contacts. It's so your friends never need to bother you for the Wi-Fi info when they come over, but it also means that if a Windows 10 user connects to my network, any of HIS Facebook/Outlook/Skype contacts get MY Wi-Fi password. If any of those people get within 100 feet of my house, what's to stop them from doing something malicious? It's incredibly easy to sniff Wi-Fi traffic and steal all of my families logins and banking information. Or maybe they'd decide to use our network as an access point to get on Silk Road and purchase some shady illegal shit? Who knows.

Past that, it's mostly just privacy concerns, and how much the way they're doing things is changing, as compared to previous versions of Windows. The things they're already doing is not a good indicator as to what's to come in the forced updates, and you lose a lot of legal protections due to how much is hosted by Microsoft. If you have any saved passwords in Internet Explorer, they get uploaded to Microsoft. If you encrypt your entire drive to keep it private using BitLocker, it automatically uploads a way to decrypt that drive, again to Microsoft's servers. That means if you ever find yourself in court for something, they could subpoena Microsoft for the decryption key, and find more stuff to charge you with during the discovery phase.

Really, all the changes aren't worth what, for me, boils down to 20 second faster boot times, and DirectX 12.
